title: Finite fibres and residue extensions of the affine Stein factor
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $f:X\to S$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and let $X\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\pi}S$ be its canonical Stein factorization [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]. For every $s\in S$, the set $\pi^{-1}(s)$ is finite, and for each $b\in\pi^{-1}(s)$ the residue field extension $\kappa(b)/\kappa(s)$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-field-extension]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] to the given proper morphism: $A\to B$ is integral, $q$ is proper, and each fibre of $q$ is nonempty. In particular $q$ is surjective. Fix $s\in S$, put $k=\kappa(s)$ and $T=\pi^{-1}(s)$ with its subspace topology. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability], distinct primes of $B$ over the prime $s$ cannot contain one another. Thus every singleton in $T$ is closed: the closure of $\{b\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ consists of primes containing $b$, and its intersection with $T$ is just $\{b\}$.

Let $Y=X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ with projection $a:Y\to X$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Proper base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] makes $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ proper, hence of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring is a field, whose only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian, without imposing anything on $A$. The fibre homeomorphism identifies $|Y|$ with $f^{-1}(s)$. Restricting $q$ gives a continuous surjection $h:|Y|\to T$: for $b\in T$ choose $z\in X$ with $q(z)=b$, then $f(z)=\pi(b)=s$, and lift $z$ by that homeomorphism.

Apply lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components to Y. Mathlib genericPoints.finite gives a finite set G of component generic points, and genericPoints.closure gives closure G = Y by lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober. The target fibre T is T1 by step 1, so the finite image h(G) is closed. Its preimage is a closed set containing G and therefore all of Y. Surjectivity of h gives T = h(G), proving finiteness, including the empty case.

Fix $b\in T$. Step 1 shows $\{b\}$ is closed in $T$, so $h^{-1}(b)$ is a nonempty closed subset of the quasi-compact scheme $Y$. Schemes are Kolmogorov: sobriety [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] gives this directly, since two points with the same singleton closure would be two generic points of that irreducible closed set. Apply [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to obtain $x\in h^{-1}(b)$ that is closed in $Y$.

Choose an affine member $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of a finite-type affine cover of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ containing $x$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $C$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Since $x$ is closed in $Y$, it is closed in $U$; its prime ideal $\mathfrak m$ is maximal, and $\kappa(x)=C/\mathfrak m$: restriction to the open neighbourhood gives the same stalk, namely $C_{\mathfrak m}$, and $C_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m C_{\mathfrak m}=(C/\mathfrak m)_{C\setminus\mathfrak m}=C/\mathfrak m$, since every element inverted has nonzero image in this field. This quotient is a field and a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to conclude $[\kappa(x):k]<\infty$. In Lean reuse the already proved source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_isClosed from WeilConjectures.PointCount for precisely this finite-residue-field assertion, rather than repeating its affine Jacobson/Zariski lemma proof.

The morphism $q\circ a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ sends $x$ to $b$, hence induces a field map $\kappa(b)\to\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. It is injective [def-pc-field-extension]. The equality $\pi\circ q\circ a=(\operatorname{Spec}k\to S)\circ(Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$ says the resulting tower $k\to\kappa(b)\to\kappa(x)$ has as composite the structure map used in step 5: this follows by composing the local ring maps and reducing modulo their maximal ideals. Thus $\kappa(b)$ embeds as a $k$-linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space $\kappa(x)$. Any linearly independent family in $\kappa(b)$ stays independent in $\kappa(x)$, so its size is at most $[\kappa(x):k]$; consequently $[\kappa(b):k]<\infty$. This proves the residue-field clause for every $b\in T$. In Lean insert Scheme.residueFieldCongr for the equality pi(a(x)) = s. Compare the composite field maps after applying Spec and composing with S.fromSpecResidueField s. Naturality of fromSpecResidueField and the pullback equation identify the composites; cancel this monomorphism and use Spec.map_injective. The private proved helper finite_left_of_comp invokes Module.Finite.left for the resulting field tower. RingHom.Finite.of_comp_finite removes the source congruence isomorphism, and transport along a(x) = b gives the stated map.
